messages:
maya: heads-up, us-west serving pool saw a sharp throughput drop ~09:14 UTC. dashboard shows worker restarts and OOMs.
alex: looking now — any correlating deploys?
deploy-bot: deploy finished: inference-runtime v2.8.1 -> v2.8.2 at 09:12 UTC (canary 10%).
maya: canary was small but spike started ~2m after canary.
ritesh: initial `nvidia-smi` logs from host-47 show fragmented free memory and repeated CUDA OOMs. pastebin: https://paste.example/frag-logs
samir: CPU looks fine, but we see kernel-swapping behavior in perf profile (higher kernel occupancy on the new binary).
alex: stepping through the profile: kernel selection path appears to pick the new matmul kernel for certain sequence lengths — those inputs are slightly longer than the usual distribution. might be a different heuristic in v2.8.2
maya: batch sizes also changed? batching config was tweaked in the rollout: window_ms reduced to 8ms to lower latency. maybe more small batches -> more kernel churn?
ritesh: from flamegraph (snippet):
```
runtime_loop -> select_kernel -> jit_compile? -> launch_kernel_A (heavy reg pressure)
runtime_loop -> kv_cache_lookup -> fallback_to_copy (more memcpy)
```
seems like KB cache path is hitting fallback copies under memory pressure.
alex: interesting — fallback_to_copy increases peak memory because it materializes KV segments. with many small batches that could blow memory for certain GPU types with low device-side free.
samir: noisy neighbor theory: other tenants on the same GPU node triggered a big allocation spike -> fragmentation -> subsequent allocations fail even if overall free memory looks ok. we saw this pattern before.
maya: can we confirm with host metrics? ritest, do we have per-tenant allocation traces?
ritesh: yes. logs show tenant 'research-batch' had a 30GB transient spike at 09:13:20. timeline: tenant spike -> fragmentation -> our requests start OOMing -> worker restart autorestart -> regen of cache warms up -> throughput drops ~30% for 6m.
alex: mitigation steps: 1) rollback canary to v2.8.1 (stop kernel change), 2) pin quantized kernel variant that uses lower temporary memory, 3) add a transient eviction of large KV entries under OOM.
maya: rolled back canary at 09:20 UTC. deploy-bot: rollback started.
deploy-bot: rollback complete at 09:22 UTC.
ritesh: after rollback, OOMs stopped, worker restarts ceased. throughput recovered to baseline by ~09:29 UTC.
samir: follow-ups: (a) add noisy-neighbor detector alert that watches transient allocations, (b) change kernel-selection heuristic to prefer lower-allo kernels when free_frag < 0.2 * total_gpu_mem, (c) adjust batching heuristic: avoid shrinking window_ms during canaries on shared nodes.
alex: also want a tiny experiment: on a small set of nodes, enable proactive compaction call in CUDA driver or preallocate scratch to reduce fragmentation.
maya: creating incident report and follow-up ticket: INC-2025-137. owners: ritest (root cause), alex (kernel heuristic), samir (scheduling/alerts).
maya: thanks all — keeping this thread for the postmortem notes. :thumbsup:
